title: Prime-to-characteristic primary order of a finite commutative group scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $G$ be a finite commutative $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Put $N=\dim_k\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$, the scheme-theoretic order, and let $\ell$ be a prime different from $\operatorname{char}k$. Write $e=v_\ell(N)$, where the integer valuation is [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Then $N\geq1$, the group $G(k)$ is finite, and its subgroup
$$G(k)[\ell^\infty]=\{x\in G(k):\ell^n x=0\text{ for some }n\geq0\}$$
has cardinality $\ell^e$. For every integer $n\geq\max(1,e)$ one has
$$\#\{x\in G(k):\ell^n x=0\}=\ell^e.$$
No reducedness or etaleness hypothesis on $G$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 11.3, printed p.210 (connected-etale splitting over a perfect field), Corollary 11.30 and Corollary 11.31, printed pp.220–221 (connected order and characteristic zero smoothness); primary subgroup cardinality is the finite abelian group consequence. This is the finite-group-scheme input in Milne AV I proof of Proposition 10.20, printed p.52.

proof.text: Apply the local–constant product decomposition to $G$. With $C$ its identity component, $d=\dim_k\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$ and $H=G(k)$ of cardinality $q$, it gives a finite connected commutative group scheme $C$, a finite group $H$, $d,q\geq1$, and $N=dq$. In particular $N\geq1$.

source.place: Proposition 11.3, printed p.210, Corollaries 11.30-11.31, printed p.220; elementary finite abelian group assembly using Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity.

proof.text: In characteristic $p>0$, $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by the field-flatness lemma. The connected finite-order theorem therefore gives $d=p^r$ for some $r\geq0$. As $\ell\ne p$, $d$ is prime to $\ell$. In characteristic zero, apply the prime-to-characteristic etaleness theorem to $G$ (its characteristic-zero clause imposes no divisibility restriction). The finite-etale-points theorem then gives $q=N$. Thus in either characteristic $v_\ell(q)=v_\ell(N)=e$: in the positive-characteristic case remove the factor $p^r$ from $N=p^r q$.

source.place: Proposition 11.3, printed p.210, Corollaries 11.30-11.31, printed p.220; elementary finite abelian group assembly using Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity.

proof.text: Put $P=\{x\in H:\ell^a x=0\text{ for some }a\geq0\}$. It contains zero. If $\ell^a x=0$ and $\ell^b y=0$, then $\ell^{a+b}(x+y)=0$; also $\ell^a(-x)=0$. Hence $P$ is a subgroup, using commutativity of $H$. Every subgroup all of whose elements are killed by some power of $\ell$ is contained in $P$, by the displayed definition. Thus $P$ is maximal among such subgroups.

source.place: Proposition 11.3, printed p.210, Corollaries 11.30-11.31, printed p.220; elementary finite abelian group assembly using Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity.

proof.text: Use multiplicative notation for the same abstract group $H$ and subgroup $P$. Step 3 verifies exactly the elementwise prime-power and maximality hypotheses of the Sylow-cardinality lemma. That lemma gives $|P|=\ell^{v_\ell(q)}=\ell^e$ by step 2. The definition of $P$ is precisely $G(k)[\ell^\infty]$.

source.place: Proposition 11.3, printed p.210, Corollaries 11.30-11.31, printed p.220; elementary finite abelian group assembly using Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity.

proof.text: The finite-group cardinal-annihilator lemma applied to $P$ shows that $\ell^e x=0$ for every $x\in P$. For $n\geq\max(1,e)$, multiply this equality by $\ell^{n-e}$ to obtain $\ell^n x=0$. Conversely, an element killed by $\ell^n$ belongs to $P$, taking $a=n$ in its definition. Hence $\{x\in G(k):\ell^n x=0\}=P$, and its cardinality is $\ell^e$. This also handles $e=0$: $P$ has one element, which is zero.

tool_uses.why: Connected order in positive characteristic is the finite-group-scheme structural input; no node of the item unit replaces this statement.
Its characteristic-zero clause supplies etaleness for the finite group scheme; no node of this unit replaces it.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q89-25abe261e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new leaf, every cited statement, Milne iAG Prop 11.3 and Cor 11.30–11.31, and Mathlib Sylow.lean 52-55 and 761-767 plus PGroup.lean 24-27. The base was unsplit with no proof, and the statement is unchanged. Step 1: the local-constant product gives N=dq, H finite, d,q≥1. Step 2: in char p, flat-field plus connected-order give d=p^r, prime to ℓ; in char 0, the étaleness clause plus finite-etale-points (Lean-closed) with k'=k give q=N. In both cases v_ℓ(q)=e. Step 2 cites flat-field for G's flatness but its text names only C, which is cosmetic. Steps 3-5: the ℓ-power torsion P is a maximal ℓ-subgroup, Sylow cardinality gives ℓ^e, and the annihilator leaf gives the n-torsion equality, including e=0. The new leaf lem-sfb-sylow-subgroup-cardinality is exactly Sylow.mk plus card_eq_multiplicity with Finite and Fact p.Prime, a one-line specialization. An rg -L sylow search found no duplicate; the existing nodes cover conjugacy or prime index only. Tested on trivial G, α_p, μ_p (e=0), (Z/ℓ)^2 and S_3. Accepted tool_uses: lem-sc-connected-finite-order and lem-sc-fg-order-prime-etale, both generic finite-group-scheme black boxes. No SGA source is used.

lean.statement: theorem finite_commutative_group_scheme_primary_order {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [IsCommMonObj G] [IsFinite G.hom] (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (hℓ : ℓ ≠ ringChar k) : 1 ≤ G.hom.finrankΓ ∧ Finite (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ G) ∧ Nat.card (CommGroup.primaryComponent (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ G) ℓ) = ℓ ^ padicValNat ℓ G.hom.finrankΓ ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, max 1 (padicValNat ℓ G.hom.finrankΓ) ≤ n → Nat.card {x : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ G // x ^ (ℓ ^ n) = 1} = ℓ ^ padicValNat ℓ G.hom.finrankΓ
